introduction: Today we celebrate the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus. Through Ezekiel, God promises to seek out his lost sheep himself and to bind up the injured. Paul tells us that God proves his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us. In the Gospel, the shepherd leaves the ninety-nine to look for the one lost sheep, and carries it home rejoicing. Let us rest in the love of the heart of Christ.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God proves his love for us in that Christ died for us while we were still sinners. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may go out to seek the lost with the heart of the Good Shepherd. Let us pray to the Lord.
For priests, on this day of prayer for their sanctification: that they may have hearts like the heart of Jesus. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are lost, injured or weak: that the Shepherd may find them, bind up their wounds and carry them home. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who feel unworthy of God's love: that they may discover that Christ died for them while they were still sinners. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may rejoice when the lost are found. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, in the heart of your Son you show us the depth of your love. Seek us when we are lost, heal us when we are wounded, and carry us home. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Rejoice with me
reflection.body:
Through the prophet Ezekiel, God makes a promise to a scattered people: "Behold, I myself, even I, will search for my sheep, and will seek them out." He does not leave this task to others. "I will seek that which was lost, and will bring back that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was sick."

In the Gospel, Jesus tells the parable of the lost sheep. A shepherd with a hundred sheep loses one. He leaves the ninety-nine and goes after the lost one "until he found it." When he finds it, he does not scold it or drive it home: "he carries it on his shoulders, rejoicing." Then he calls his friends: "Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost!" And Jesus explains: "there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance."

This is the heart of Jesus: a heart that cannot rest while one person is lost, and that rejoices when they are found.

Paul tells us how far that love goes. "For one will hardly die for a righteous man." But Christ died for us when we did not deserve it: "God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us." God did not wait for us to become good before loving us. And Paul assures us that "hope doesn't disappoint us, because God's love has been poured into our hearts."

The devotion to the Sacred Heart invites us to trust this love completely. This week, if you feel lost or far from God, let Jesus find you and carry you. And if you know someone who has wandered away, pray for them, and rejoice when they come home.
